source.section: Schedule M line 34 Social Security Benefits, 100% at or under the AGI limit and 65% above it for 2025 (PDF p.5; instructions PDF p.28; PDF p.17; Tax Division Social Security Modification page); Schedule M line 47 Senior Citizen Deduction columns (a)-(d) (PDF p.6; instructions PDF p.29; example PDF p.30; PDF p.23 'Taxpayers over age 65 or disabled'; Tax Division page: 'You receive the higher of the $8,000 modification or the sum of various itemized decreasing modifications'); IT-140 lines 1-8 (PDF p.3; instructions PDF p.26: exemptions 2,000 each, line 7 floored at zero); Rate Schedules I and II (PDF p.37); Tax Table (PDF p.38 on)

worked: Single, age 69, federal AGI over 50,000: line 34 is 65% of the taxable benefits, and column (d) uses that 65% figure, so line 47 tops it up to 8,000. filer born 1956-03-01, age 69 at December 31, 2025. Federal taxable Social Security (IRS worksheet, given): other income 50,000.00 + half of benefits 5,000.00 = provisional income 55,000.00; 85% x (55,000.00 - 34,000.00) = 17,850.00 + lesser of 4,500.00 and half the benefits 5,000.00 = 22,350.00, limited to 85% of benefits 8,500.00: 8,500.00. Federal AGI (given) = private pension 50,000.00 + taxable Social Security 8,500.00 = 58,500.00. Federal taxable income (given, not tested) = 58,500.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 aged 65 or older = 40,750.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). IT-140 line 1 federal AGI 58,500.00. Schedule M additions lines 51-58 none; IT-140 line 2 0.00. Schedule M Column A: line 34(a) total benefits 10,000.00, (b) exempt for federal 1,500.00, (c) taxable 8,500.00; federal AGI 58,500.00 exceeds 50,000.00, so line 34 = 0.65 x 8,500.00 = 5,525.00; line 47 (age 69): column (c) income not on lines 35-46 = 58,500.00, limited to 8,000.00: 8,000.00; column (d) lines 29-34 = 5,525.00; line 47 = 8,000.00 - 5,525.00 = 2,475.00; line 49 = 8,000.00. Line 50 total subtractions = 8,000.00. Projection (per person): The filer: Social Security subtraction 5,525.00; age 65 deduction = lesser of (8,000.00 - military retirement 0.00) and own income 58,500.00 = 8,000.00; best_of_group wv_line_47 keeps the larger, 8,000.00 (wv_senior_citizen_deduction). Projection subtractions total 8,000.00, the same as line 50. IT-140 line 3 subtractions 8,000.00; line 4 West Virginia AGI = 58,500.00 + 0.00 - 8,000.00 = 50,500.00. Line 5 Low-Income Earned Income Exclusion: federal AGI over 10,000, none. Line 6 exemptions 1 x 2,000.00 = 2,000.00. Line 7 taxable income = 50,500.00 - 2,000.00 = 48,500.00. Line 8 tax by Rate Schedule I (PDF p.37) bands: 2.22% x 10,000.00 = 222 + 2.96% x 15,000.00 = 444 + 3.33% x 15,000.00 = 499.5 + 4.44% x 8,500.00 = 377.4; total 1542.9 = 1,542.90. The Tax Table row 48,500 to under 48,550 (PDF p.38 on) gives 1,544; expected keeps the schedule formula on the exact income. No Family Tax Credit (Modified Federal AGI above the table limits); credits 0.00; state income tax 1,542.90.
accepted_approximations: Tax below 100,000 of taxable income is figured on the exact income, where the booklet uses a Tax Table row's midpoint rounded to the whole dollar. Other tax is also rounded to the whole dollar in the booklet.
